messages:
maria: Quiet flag: noticed a ~20% tail-latency spike on p95 after yesterday's scheduler-affinity change (commit 9f4a2b1). Putting up traces.

maria: nsys capture: https://artifacts.internal/nsys/2465012345/9f4a2b1.before.nsys
maria: nsys capture after revert patch: https://artifacts.internal/nsys/2465012345/9f4a2b1.after.nsys

ajay: Thanks — rough time window? CI nightly or prod ramp?

maria: Prod ramp on canary at 15:02 UTC. CI reprobed locally with 1k requests/min and got the same p95 shift.

cheng: Any obvious kernel timeline shift? kernel hop / different kernel chosen?

maria: Yeah. In the before/after flame timeline I see the compute kernel switching from fast_linear_attn to fallback_attn for long sequences starting around 1200 steps.

maria: Paste of nsys excerpt:
```
Time(ms)  Kernel                Queue  Duration(ms)
1203.1    fast_linear_attn      2      0.48
1203.6    fallback_attn         2      3.21   <-- regressed
1210.9    memcopy_h2d           1      0.30
```

sam: That sounds like kernel-selector picked a different kernel because of affinity change? Maybe the per-stream resource hints are different.

maria: Hypothesis: scheduler-affinity patch changed GPU stream sequencing and increased concurrent seq-length variance -> changed heuristics in kernel selector -> chose lower-throughput kernel for those batch shapes.

perf-bot: Automated diff: p95 +18%, avg token time +12%, KV cache hit ratio -1.2% on canary (details at https://perf.internal/diffs/2465012345)

cheng: Ok let's bisect. Plan: run git bisect on the runtime commits between 9f4a2b1^ and 9f4a2b1 with a tiny harness that replays a failing perfetto trace and captures nsys. I can script this.

maria: I already started a local bisect script. Command I used:
```
git bisect start --term-old=good --term-new=bad
git bisect run ./tools/run_perf_repro.sh --profile nsys --warmup 50 --requests 1000
```

maria: First bad commit landed at 9f4a2b1, but bisect shows the change is actually 9d3c4e7 which touches scheduler.cpp (stream affinity pruning).

ajay: Can you paste the perfetto link of the before/after kernel timeline zoomed to 1195-1215 ms? I want to look at GPU queue starvations.

maria: perfetto snippet: https://perfetto.internal/viewer/trace/2465012345#1200-1215

emma: Noticed also a tiny uptick in KV cache eviction during the window — maybe prefetch ordering changed because of stream impacts.

sam: If kernel selector uses sequence-length histograms it could be sensitive to the order of requests hitting the batcher. Affinity altering threading could change request ordering.

maria: Reproduced by applying a minimal patch that restores previous stream pinning; p95 falls back to baseline. So root cause likely scheduler stream assignment.

cheng: For fix, either revert affinity pruning or make kernel-selector robust to interleaved sequence-length distributions. Short-term revert + unit test for order invariance.

ajay: Agree. Create PR with revert + perf test harness run in CI. Tag me for review.

maria: Filed PR #5124 with revert + nsys baseline artifact. I'll also attach the bisect log. cc @ajay @cheng :thumbsup:

perf-bot: CI perf test queued for PR #5124. Will post results when done.

maria: thanks all — next: monitor canary for 2 hours post-merge and then roll to prod if clean :rocket:
